subject: Clarify default retention for request/response and generated content
messages:

Subject: Question on retention — what Redwood keeps by default?

Chloe, thanks for the demo earlier. Procurement has a couple of quick questions we need answered to move the SOW through our review:

1) By default, what logs does Redwood persist for hosted API customers? Specifically: are customer prompts stored? are model outputs stored? what about request/response payloads and full traces?
2) What is the default retention period for those items (if any)?
3) Can BrightBank request immediate deletion/purge of our historical requests and outputs? What's the process and SLA for that?
4) Will Redwood use our prompts or outputs to train models or improve public models if we're on the hosted plan?
5) We need a one-page statement we can attach to the procurement packet confirming the above and listing any exceptions (billing/audit traces).

Appreciate a short, plain-language answer we can give to legal and procurement today.

—Sarah

Head of Cloud Security, BrightBank

Subject: Re: Question on retention — what Redwood keeps by default?

Hi Sarah — thanks, appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, then quick details below.

TL;DR (plain-language summary you can use in procurement):
- Default (hosted API): Redwood retains request metadata and request payloads (prompts) and service-level responses for 45 days by default.
- Generated outputs (model responses) are considered transient by default: they are not persisted as long-lived artifacts unless a customer opts into logging, uses features that persist outputs (e.g., Redwood Optimize checkpoints, long-term evaluations), or stores them via their own export.
- Billing and security audit logs (aggregated telemetry, token counts, error traces) are retained for longer for billing and incident investigation, but those are not full content dumps.
- Customers on Dedicated or Private plans can configure retention and residency to meet contracts (e.g., zero retention or EU-only residency).
- We do not use customer prompts/outputs from hosted accounts for model training unless explicitly opted-in via a written agreement (we can add this clause to the DPA/SOW).

More detail:
1) What we store by default (hosted API):
   • Request metadata (timestamps, route, client-id) — stored for operational/debugging and billing.
   • Request payloads (prompts and any user-supplied context) — retained up to 45 days by default to support debugging, quality regressions, and abuse investigations.
   • Streaming caches (KV cache, session prefixes) — short-lived and typically expire within session boundaries; not persisted beyond the configured TTL unless the customer enables persistence.
   • Generated token streams (model outputs): not persisted as curated, long-term artifacts by default. Temporary buffering for streaming is required but flushed per session.

2) Deletion / purge path:
   • Customers may request immediate deletion via the support portal or their account rep. We validate the request and, for hosted customers, perform a purge that removes content from primary stores and schedules tombstone removal across replicas. The visible confirmation is typically within 72 hours; final tombstone purge can take up to 14 days depending on replication and backups.
   • For Dedicated/Private, runbook and timeline are contract defined and can include immediate irrevocable wipes if required.

3) Residency & EU data:
   • By default hosted traffic is stored in the region you choose at account creation when that option is supported. For strict EU residency, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments; we can provide a residency addendum for the SOW.

4) Legal / training usage:
   • We do not train public models on customer content without opt-in. Our standard DPA explicitly states training is not performed absent consent.

I'll attach a one-page retention summary and the procurement checklist you can drop into your packet. If procurement wants a signed statement in the SOW we can provide a standard clause; Marissa can confirm the wording.

Adding a few compliance/legal clarifications for procurement to consider (short bullets):

• Backups: we maintain operational backups for disaster recovery. These are not used for model training and are subject to the same data access controls; final deletion from backups is part of our backup retention schedule and may extend beyond the primary-store purge window — we will list an exact backup expiration in the SOW if BrightBank requires a shorter window.
• PII/regulated data: customers should follow our guidance on tokenization and field redaction. If you designate data as regulated in the contract, we can enact additional controls (encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys, restricted SRE access, HSM/KMS).
• Audit logs: full audit records for admin actions (who accessed the console, config changes) are retained for 1 year by default for enterprise tenancy; aggregated telemetry for service health is retained longer but content is obfuscated.
• Deletion verification: for procurement needs, we can provide a deletion certificate (signed statement) after we complete the purge process.

If procurement needs explicit contractual language (e.g., confirmation that outputs are not stored), we recommend the following sentence in the SOW: "Redwood Inference will not use Customer content for model training and will not persist generated outputs or prompt content beyond the agreed retention period unless the Customer has opted into content logging or storage features."

Happy to iterate on exact wording.

—Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
